sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's digital infrastructure names (DCII, NFCX) benefit from accelerating data-center capex tied to domestic AI and cloud adoption, a multi-year demand cycle independent of US rate swings.
Local listings like BELI and PGJO ride a retail-driven IPO momentum wave, but sustainability hinges on post-lockup earnings delivery, making selectivity critical.
US tech drag (-2.21%) pressures IDX tech via sentiment contagion, yet local names with domestic revenue (WGSH, RCCC) show resilience, favoring a barbell of pure-play local and defensive US laggards.
sectors.ai: Buy BELI on its +24.5% breakout as the sole high-conviction tech name, but avoid chasing PGJO/UVCR given thin liquidity. Trim US-exposed DCII/HPQ into strength; rotate into NFCX for data-center leverage. Overall, keep tech underweight—ID strength is stock-specific, not sectoral—and wait for a US tech stabilization signal before adding beta.

sectors.ai: Buy the pullback in high-growth digital banks (ARTO, BANK) and niche lenders (BSIM, NOBU) on strength, as the sector's domestic outperformance (+0.67% ID vs -1.07% US) signals resilient local liquidity and risk appetite. Rotate out of laggards with no catalyst; hold diversified insurers (LIFE, ASBI) for upside. Target BSIM and LIFE for momentum continuation into next week, but trim on any 5%+ spike to lock gains.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US utility deregulation and grid investment cycles are decoupling from renewables pure-plays, favoring integrated operators with rate-base growth.
Indonesia's energy transition hinges on JETP disbursement and PLN procurement reforms, creating binary upside for listed IPPs like ESSA and BATR.
Climate-tech valuations are compressing globally, but carbon capture and geothermal niches in Indonesia offer outsized structural returns as policy clarity improves.
sectors.ai: Buy selective US utility/clean-power names (EIX, PCG, SRE) on rate-cut tailwinds and grid-hardening capex; Indonesia renewables remain policy-driven and lagging—overweight only ESSA/BATR on near-term earnings visibility. Rotate out of CEG if power-price volatility spikes.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Palm-oil upstream integration is re-rating consumer conglomerates as CPO prices stay elevated, rewarding BWPT and GZCO with margin expansion beyond packaged-goods exposure.
Mid-cap FMCG distributors (SSMS, FLMC) are capturing rural demand recovery via expanded SKU penetration, a structural shift as logistics costs normalize post-election.
Defensive staples lag as US rate differentials pressure IDR, pushing investors toward export-earning consumer names over domestic-demand pure plays.
sectors.ai: Buy selective consumer names with hard-asset or export leverage (BWPT, SSMS) while avoiding pure domestic staples; the sector's flat aggregate masks strong idiosyncratic rallies, so rotate into palm-linked FMCG and liquid cash-flow plays ahead of rupiah stability and subsidy policy clarity.

US managed-care names (CVS, ELV, HUM) face persistent regulatory and margin-compression risks, making them tactical, not core, holdings for Indonesia-focused portfolios.

Add CVS/ELV/HUM only as defensive hedges against US policy noise. Rotate out of laggards into names with pricing power and government contract visibility.
